label: Guided walkthrough
disclaimer: This guided script describes the verified release named on the page. It is not a live Veasel session, recorded model run, or benchmark. The terminal recording is authentic CLI/TUI output and makes no model calls.

steps.title: Install a verified preview
steps.summary: Grab a checksummed archive or a package manager build that tracks the same tag.
steps.prompt: Get Veasel onto PATH without inventing a release.

lines.text: # Verify SHA-256 before you run (downloads page links SHA256SUMS)
veasel --version
Veasel Code {{version}}
veasel
# starts or reuses 127.0.0.1:4097, then opens the TUI

steps.note: Homebrew and AUR install the same verified archives listed on Downloads.

steps.title: Connect a provider
steps.summary: Choose a provider such as OpenCode Go, paste its API key once, and keep credentials local.
steps.prompt: Choose OpenCode Go and authenticate without sending keys back through the API.

lines.text: /connect
OpenCode Go → paste API key → discover models → choose one
/models
Ctrl+U endpoint · Ctrl+O output budget · keys never re-shown

steps.title: Open a workspace session
steps.summary: Bind a session to a real directory; history stays in local SQLite.
steps.prompt: Ask about the repo with bounded list/read/search tools.

lines.text: Home · j/k move · Enter open · n new when empty
Where do we configure the loopback API port?
I’ll search the workspace, then cite the matching files.
workspace.search "4097" → pending review of results in context

steps.note: Tool excerpts may be sent to your configured provider — local storage is not local inference.

steps.title: Review a file edit
steps.summary: Edits are proposals until you inspect and approve.
steps.prompt: Nothing lands on disk until approve.

lines.text: Change ready · src/config.v · +6 −2
/patches
Ctrl+R
Select an edit to inspect its diff, then approve or reject it.
# rejected or interrupted edits are not replayed

steps.note: Diff reviews lead with add/remove counts and keep the decision on the first screen.

steps.title: Approve a shell command
steps.summary: Shell shows the exact command, cwd, timeout, and sandbox wrap.
steps.prompt: Authorize one command — not a blank check.

lines.text: /commands
Select a command to inspect its exact text and execution details.
cwd ~/project · timeout 60s · sandbox bubblewrap (when available)
Approve or reject from the review panel after inspection.

steps.note: Platform sandboxes are defense-in-depth; approval remains the authorization gate.

steps.title: Configure and review MCP
steps.summary: User or project scope, portable .mcp.json import, then trust + per-call approval.
steps.prompt: Tools stay visible — every call pauses.

lines.text: veasel mcp add stdio memory npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory
veasel mcp add project http docs https://mcp.example.com/mcp
# or drop workspace .mcp.json / .cursor/mcp.json (read-only import)
/mcp trust configured/memory
Ctrl+R
Select an MCP call to inspect and approve or reject it.

steps.note: The default Solid TUI lists and trusts servers; configure servers with the headless veasel mcp commands. Each tool call still needs review.

steps.title: Run headless when you need a script
steps.summary: Same approvals and API — machine-readable JSON for automation.
steps.prompt: Keep the harness honest: no invented scores.

lines.text: veasel run --prompt "List the top-level modules" --workspace . --json
{"ok":true,"session_id":"…","usage_reported":true}
# Harbor adapter uses veasel run inside Bubblewrap + verified Linux release

steps.note: Harbor Index is still Not submitted (auth + human PR + budget blockers on /evals/). A sanitized ATIF smoke sample from the mock-provider path is linked there — plumbing only, not a score.
